src/server.ts binds the app to the PORT env var (default 3001) and src/app.ts assembles the express app and middleware.

userStories.title: Wire JWT Dual Token Bootstrap And Guard Middleware
userStories.description: Wire the minimum authentication foundation in apps/api: a token service issuing the access + refresh dual-token pair and a requireAuth middleware protecting routes. This establishes the dual-rotation strategy before any auth endpoint or page exists.
acceptanceCriteria: src/auth/token.service.ts exposes signAccessToken(userId, role, tenantId) and signRefreshToken(userId); access tokens are signed with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET (default TTL 15m) and refresh tokens with JWT_REFRESH_SECRET (default TTL 30d), each carrying a type claim of access or refresh and a unique jti.
The two token streams are enforced distinct: requireAuth accepts ONLY type=access tokens, and a refresh token presented to a protected route is rejected with 401.

requireAuth middleware attaches req.user (userId, role, tenantId) on success and rejects missing, malformed, expired, or wrong-type tokens with 401 body {success: false, message: 'Unauthorized', data: null}.
A protected test route GET /health-protected guarded by requireAuth returns 401 with no token, 200 with the success envelope for a valid access token, and 401 for a valid refresh token.
Unit tests cover the sign/verify round-trip, the wrong-type rejection, and the expired-token rejection for both token kinds.
Integration tests with supertest cover all three /health-protected outcomes listed above.

A Node script scripts/check-env-coverage.ts scans apps/api/src for process.env.<VAR> reads and fails (exit 1) if any read is missing from .env.example; the script runs and passes under the apps/api test suite.

userStories.title: Wire Azure Blob Storage Client Factory

The container client exposes the block-blob upload surface (createBlockBlob / uploadBlockFromStream) that later multipart upload endpoints will call, verified by a unit test asserting the methods exist on the returned client.

userStories.title: Define Tenant And User Models In Prisma Schema
userStories.description: Extend the Prisma schema in apps/api (initialized by STORY-setup-006) with the Tenant and User models exactly as the data-model dictionary specifies. Tenant holds a UUID primary key and a name; User holds a UUID primary key, unique email, unique username, passwordHash, firstName, lastName, isActive (default true), isDeleted (default false), requirePasswordChange, and Timestamptz(3) audit timestamps. No cross-model relations are declared in this story; relations arrive with the later model stories.
acceptanceCriteria: The Prisma schema defines model Tenant with `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `name String`, `createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @db.Timestamptz(3)`, and `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @db.Timestamptz(3)`.

The Prisma schema defines model User with `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `email String @unique`, `username String @unique`, `passwordHash String`, `firstName String`, `lastName String`, `isActive Boolean @default(true)`, `isDeleted Boolean @default(false)`, `requirePasswordChange Boolean`, plus Timestamptz(3) createdAt/updatedAt.
No relations to other models are declared on Tenant or User in this story, keeping the contract exactly as specified.
Running `npx prisma validate` from apps/api completes with exit code 0.
Running `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_tenant_user` from apps/api completes with exit code 0 and `npx prisma generate` succeeds.
Integration test in apps/api (Jest, Prisma client) creates a Tenant and a User, then asserts that inserting a second User with the same email throws a Prisma P2002 unique-constraint error.

userStories.title: Define TenantUser Role Enum And Customer Models
userStories.description: Add the Role enum and the tenancy plus CRM domain to the Prisma schema: TenantUser (tenant membership with role and the composite unique [tenantId, userId]), Customer (tenant-scoped CRM record with optional sales person), and CustomerDocument (customer file references). The optional mutual TenantUser.customerId to Customer and Customer.salesPersonId to TenantUser relation is circular by design and is resolved inside this single schema change and migration.
acceptanceCriteria: The Prisma schema declares `enum Role` with exactly nine values: SUPER_ADMIN, OFFICE_ADMIN, STAFF, SALES_PERSON, PRICING_COURIER, PRICING_AIR_SEA, CS_COURIER, CS_AIR_SEA, CUSTOMER.
model TenantUser has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `tenantId` FK to Tenant, `userId` FK to User, `role Role`, nullable `customerId String?` FK to Customer, and `@@unique([tenantId, userId])`.

model Customer has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `tenantId` FK to Tenant, `companyName String`, `contactPerson String`, nullable `email String?`, nullable `salesPersonId String?` FK to TenantUser, and `isDeleted Boolean`.
model CustomerDocument has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `customerId` FK to Customer, `type String`, and `fileUrl String`.

The circular optional TenantUser.customerId / Customer.salesPersonId relation compiles: `npx prisma validate` exits 0 and `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_membership_and_customers` completes with exit code 0 followed by `npx prisma generate`.

Integration test (Jest, Prisma client) creates a Tenant, a User, a TenantUser with role SALES_PERSON, and a Customer with salesPersonId set, then asserts the composite unique constraint rejects a second TenantUser with the same (tenantId, userId) via a P2002 error.
All DateTime fields on TenantUser, Customer, and CustomerDocument (createdAt/updatedAt) carry `@db.Timestamptz(3)`.

userStories.title: Define RefreshToken Model For Dual Token Rotation
userStories.description: Add the RefreshToken model that persists the state behind the project's access/refresh dual-token strategy: a unique hashed (never plaintext) token, its owning User, a revocation flag, an optional anti-collision jti, and an expiry timestamp. This model is what lets rotation issue, revoke, and validate refresh tokens against the database instead of in memory.
acceptanceCriteria: model RefreshToken has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `hashedToken String @unique`, `userId` FK to User, `isRevoked Boolean @default(false)`, nullable `jti String?` (UUID), and `expiresAt DateTime @db.Timestamptz(3)`.
The refresh token is persisted only as `hashedToken` - the model has no plaintext token column, so raw tokens never reach the database.
`jti` is nullable and serves anti-collision tracking of issued tokens, so a reissued or colliding token can be detected.

Integration test (Jest, Prisma client) issues two RefreshTokens for the same User, revokes the first (isRevoked = true), and asserts a query for active tokens (isRevoked = false) returns exactly the second token - the persistence contract behind dual-token rotation.
`npx prisma migrate dev --name add_refresh_token` completes with exit code 0 and `npx prisma generate` succeeds.

userStories.title: Define Job Model With Sequence And Status
userStories.description: Add the Job model: a tenant-scoped logistics job with an autoincrementing jobSequence, a globally unique jobCode, an owning Customer, a name, a status that defaults to OPEN, and an isConfidential flag. The tenantId foreign key is the multi-tenant binding that isolates Jobs per Tenant.
acceptanceCriteria: model Job has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `tenantId` FK to Tenant, `jobSequence Int @default(autoincrement())`, `jobCode String @unique`, `customerId` FK to Customer, `name String`, `status String @default("OPEN")`, `isConfidential Boolean @default(false)`, plus Timestamptz(3) createdAt/updatedAt.
Every Job row carries a `tenantId` foreign key to its owning Tenant - the multi-tenant binding that isolates Jobs per tenant.
Integration test (Jest, Prisma client) creates a Job for a Customer under a Tenant, then asserts that inserting a second Job with the same jobCode throws a P2002 unique-constraint error.
Integration test asserts a Job created without an explicit status persists with status OPEN and isConfidential false.
`npx prisma migrate dev --name add_job` completes with exit code 0 and `npx prisma generate` succeeds.

userStories.title: Define Recursive JobFolder And JobFile Models
userStories.description: Add the nested file structure: JobFolder with a self-referential nullable parentId (recursive OS-style nesting, no materialized path) and JobFile linking to an optional folder and job. A root folder has parentId null; child folders point at their parent, and files hang off any folder or the job itself.
acceptanceCriteria: model JobFolder has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `name String`, `jobId` FK to Job, `folderSequence Int`, `folderCode String`, and a nullable self-referential `parentId String?` FK to JobFolder declared under an explicit relation name (e.g. `@relation("FolderParent")`).

model JobFile has `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `name String`, `blobUrl String`, `sizeBytes Int`, `mimeType String`, nullable `jobId String?` FK to Job, and nullable `folderId String?` FK to JobFolder.

Integration test (Jest, Prisma client) creates a root JobFolder under a Job (parentId null), a child JobFolder (parentId = root id), and a JobFile (folderId = child id), then asserts a nested Prisma include from the root resolves root to child to file.
Nesting is expressed only via the recursive `parentId` - JobFolder has no materialized-path, slug-path, or ancestors-array column.
`npx prisma migrate dev --name add_job_folder_file` completes with exit code 0 and `npx prisma generate` succeeds.

`npx prisma migrate status` reports all migrations applied with no pending changes against the PostgreSQL database.
`npm test` in apps/api runs the data-model integration suite with exit code 0.

userStories.title: Establish Global SCSS Design Tokens And Frosted-Glass Theme
userStories.description: Create the global SCSS design-token layer for apps/web: a `.glass-surface` class applying `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)` over a semi-transparent background (the frosted-glass boundary for modals and floating cards) and a `.mesh-bg` class applying an animated `radial-gradient()` mesh background reusable by the auth-shell and 404 views, plus CSS custom properties for brand colors and blur values. This is the visual foundation every later feature page (login, change-password, staff, profile, 404) consumes. Layout uses Bootstrap 5 `.row`/`.col` structural grid only; no Tailwind, no Bootstrap text-color utilities, no default browser input styling. It calls no backend endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/web/src/styles/design-tokens.scss exists and is imported into the global styles.scss; running `npm run build` in apps/web completes with exit code 0.

A `.glass-surface` SCSS class applies `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)` (and `-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`) over a semi-transparent background (e.g. rgba(255,255,255,0.65)), defining the frosted-glass boundary for modals and floating cards.

A `.mesh-bg` SCSS class applies an animated `radial-gradient()` mesh (multiple radial-gradient layers plus a keyframe animation on background-position/background-size) that is reusable by the auth-shell and 404 views.
CSS custom properties (e.g. `--glass-blur: 16px`, `--brand-*` color tokens) are defined so components reference tokens instead of hard-coded values.
Layout convention is pinned to Bootstrap 5 `.row`/`.col` structural grid only: no Bootstrap text-color utilities (`.text-*`) and no Tailwind classes, and no unstyled default browser inputs.
A unit test asserts design-tokens.scss compiles (Sass) without errors and that the `.glass-surface` rule contains `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`.

userStories.title: Implement Customer List Endpoint With Server-Side Pagination
userStories.description: Implement GET /api/customers in the Express API (apps/api) as the Customer controller and customers router, returning server-side paginated active customers in the uniform {success, message, data} envelope. Query parameters: page (int >= 1, default 1), pageSize (int 1-100, default 25), search (optional case-insensitive companyName substring). data shape is { items: CustomerDto[], total: number, page: number, pageSize: number } where CustomerDto is { id, tenantId, companyName, contactPerson, email, salesPersonId, salesPerson: { id, firstName, lastName, email } | null, isDeleted }. Consumed by the Customer Directory page at /customers (STORY-customer-006) via apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts listCustomers().
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: GET /api/customers with a valid Bearer access token and page=1&pageSize=25 returns 200 with body { success: true, message: string, data: { items, total, page, pageSize } } where each item has the CustomerDto shape and salesPerson is null or an object with id, firstName, lastName, email.
Only customers with isDeleted = false and tenantId equal to the token's tenant are returned; a seeded customer belonging to a second tenant never appears.
For a CUSTOMER-role token, the response is filtered to the single customer whose id equals that TenantUser.customerId (User ownership constraint); other tenant customers are invisible.
Missing or invalid page/pageSize fall back to page=1, pageSize=25; pageSize > 100 is clamped to 100 without an error response.
A request with no Bearer token or an invalid/expired token returns 401 with the uniform envelope and no raw stack trace.
Prisma P2002 (unique constraint violation) and other Prisma errors are caught and mapped to a 400 (or safe 500) uniform envelope response — never a raw untyped 500 trace leak.
Unit tests in apps/api/src/customers/customers.service.test.ts cover the active-only filter, tenant scoping, search matching, and the CUSTOMER-role ownership filter.

userStories.title: Implement Customer Detail Fetch Endpoint With Ownership Isolation
userStories.description: Add GET /api/customers/:id to the customers controller created in STORY-customer-001, returning one active customer by uuid id for the Customer Detail page at /customers/:id. The response data is the full CustomerDto (including the resolved salesPerson object when assigned). Unknown ids, soft-deleted customers, and cross-tenant ids return 404; CUSTOMER-role tokens may only fetch the customer they are mapped to via TenantUser.customerId. Consumed by apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts getCustomer(id) from CustomerDetailComponent.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: GET /api/customers/:id with a valid token for an existing active customer in the token's tenant returns 200 with { success: true, message, data } where data has id, tenantId, companyName, contactPerson, email, salesPersonId, salesPerson, and isDeleted.
When a sales person is assigned, data.salesPerson is { id, firstName, lastName, email } resolved through TenantUser.userId; when unassigned it is null.
An unknown uuid, a customer with isDeleted = true, or a customer from another tenant returns 404 with the uniform envelope — never 500 and never a cross-tenant record.
A CUSTOMER-role token receives 404 unless TenantUser.customerId equals the requested id (ownership isolation).
A request without a Bearer token or with an invalid token returns 401 with the uniform envelope.
Unit tests cover tenant scoping, the CUSTOMER-role ownership filter, and all 404 paths in customers.service.test.ts.

userStories.title: Implement Customer Create Endpoint With Sales Person Resolution
userStories.description: Add POST /api/customers to the customers controller. Request body: { companyName: string (required, min 1), contactPerson: string (required, min 1), email: string (optional), salesPersonEmail: string (optional) }. The sec-009 section declares no staff-list endpoint, so the sales person is assigned by email: salesPersonEmail must exactly match an active non-CUSTOMER TenantUser in the token's tenant, whose id is stored in salesPersonId; a blank/omitted value leaves salesPersonId null; no match is a 400. The created customer is scoped to the token's tenant with isDeleted = false and returned in the uniform envelope with 201. Consumed by apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts createCustomer() from the Add Customer modal (STORY-customer-007).
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: POST /api/customers with { companyName, contactPerson } and a SUPER_ADMIN/OFFICE_ADMIN/STAFF token returns 201 with { success: true, message, data } where data is the created CustomerDto with isDeleted = false and a generated uuid id.
Missing or empty companyName or contactPerson returns 400 with success: false and a message naming the offending field; no record is created.

A salesPersonEmail that does not match an active non-CUSTOMER TenantUser in the token's tenant returns 400 with message 'Sales person email not found in this tenant'; no record is created and nothing is partially written.
A matching salesPersonEmail sets salesPersonId to that TenantUser's id and data.salesPerson resolves to that user's { id, firstName, lastName, email }.
A CUSTOMER-role token receives 403 on this endpoint (customer creation is limited to SUPER_ADMIN, OFFICE_ADMIN, and STAFF roles); a request without or with an invalid token receives 401.

All errors use the uniform envelope; Prisma errors including P2002 are mapped to 400-safe responses with no raw 500 trace leak; unit tests cover valid creation, empty-field rejection, and cross-tenant salesPersonEmail rejection.

userStories.title: Implement Customer Update Endpoint With Partial Patch Validation
userStories.description: Add PUT /api/customers/:id to the customers controller for editing an existing customer from the detail page at /customers/:id. Request body is a partial patch: { companyName?, contactPerson?, email?, salesPersonEmail? } with at least one non-empty field required; any provided companyName or contactPerson must be non-empty. salesPersonEmail follows the STORY-customer-003 resolution rules, and an explicit blank value clears the assignment (salesPersonId = null). Only the provided fields change; the response is the updated CustomerDto with 200 in the uniform envelope. Consumed by apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts updateCustomer(id, patch) from the detail page Save button (STORY-customer-009).
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: PUT /api/customers/:id with { companyName: 'New Name' } and an admin token returns 200 with the updated CustomerDto; contactPerson, email, and salesPersonId are unchanged.
An empty body or a body whose fields are all empty/whitespace returns 400 with success: false and a message; nothing is updated.
A provided empty companyName or contactPerson returns 400; a salesPersonEmail that fails resolution returns 400 with 'Sales person email not found in this tenant' and no partial mutation occurs.
A blank or omitted salesPersonEmail that is explicitly sent as an empty string sets salesPersonId to null (assignment cleared); a matching email updates salesPersonId accordingly.
An unknown id, a customer with isDeleted = true, or a customer from another tenant returns 404 with the uniform envelope.

A CUSTOMER-role token receives 403; no/invalid token receives 401; Prisma errors including P2002 map to 400-safe uniform envelope responses with no raw trace leak; unit tests cover partial update, empty-patch rejection, and cross-tenant 404.

userStories.title: Implement Customer Delete Endpoint With Job Conflict Check
userStories.description: Add DELETE /api/customers/:id to the customers controller. Per sec-009, deletions trigger strict conflict testing that prevents cascade obliteration: if the customer has one or more Job records, deletion is blocked with 409 and nothing changes; otherwise the customer is soft-deleted (isDeleted = true — the row is never physically removed and no cascade fires on Jobs, CustomerDocuments, or folders/files). The success response is 200 with the uniform envelope and data = { id }. Consumed by apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts deleteCustomer(id) from the Delete row action on /customers (STORY-customer-008).
acceptanceCriteria: Integration test: DELETE /api/customers/:id with an admin token for a customer with no Jobs returns 200 with { success: true, message, data: { id } } and the customer's isDeleted flag becomes true while the row still exists in the database.
A customer with one or more Job records receives 409 with success: false and message 'Cannot delete customer: existing jobs reference it.'; the customer and its jobs remain unchanged.
An unknown id, an already soft-deleted customer, or a customer from another tenant returns 404 with the uniform envelope.
A CUSTOMER-role token receives 403; a request without or with an invalid token receives 401.
A soft-deleted customer no longer appears in GET /api/customers results (asserted in the same integration test as criterion 1).
Unit tests cover the job-count conflict check (jobs present blocks, jobs absent allows) and the soft-delete path; no Prisma error, including P2002, ever leaks a raw 500 trace.

userStories.title: Build Customer Directory Page With Paginated Table And Search
userStories.description: Build the Customer Directory page as Angular standalone component CustomersComponent at route /customers in apps/web, per the approved design for /customers (sidebar navigation, search/filter bar, server-paginated customer table, Add Customer modal trigger, customer name link to detail). Create the canonical service module apps/web/src/services/customerApi.ts with listCustomers({ page, pageSize, search }) → GET /api/customers, attaching the Bearer token read from the localStorage key 'nm_access_token'. The page also hosts the shared layout shell with the sidebar, which later feature stories extend. The Delete row action is added by STORY-customer-008 and the Add Customer modal by STORY-customer-007.
acceptanceCriteria: Route '/customers' is registered in the app's shared router config (apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts) mapped to CustomersComponent; visiting /customers renders the page, not a 404 or blank screen. No second router is created.

The page renders inside the shared layout shell at apps/web/src/app/layout/layout.component.ts; if that shell does not exist yet, create it with a sidebar containing a 'Customers' link (href /customers) — later feature stories add their links to this same sidebar, never a second shell.
customerApi.ts exposes listCustomers({ page, pageSize, search }) calling GET /api/customers with query params page, pageSize, search and the Authorization header 'Bearer <nm_access_token>'.
On load the table fetches page 1 (pageSize 25) and renders one row per customer with columns 'Company' (name link), 'Contact Person', and 'Email'.
The companyName cell is a link that navigates to /customers/:id in the same tab; each row also renders a 'Jobs' anchor with target="_blank" and href="/jobs?customerId=<customer id>".

The search/filter bar sends search=<text> and resets to page 1; 'Prev' and 'Next' pagination buttons change the page param and refetch; the 'Add Customer' button (exact label) is rendered in the toolbar above the table.

While the request is in flight the table shows a loading state; on 4xx/5xx the response envelope's message is displayed; when nm_access_token is absent the table area shows 'Sign in to load customers' with a 'Sign In' link to /login.

userStories.title: Implement tenant-scoped GET /api/dashboard/summary aggregation endpoint
userStories.description: Add dashboard.controller.ts to the Express API exposing GET /api/dashboard/summary. The endpoint computes tenant-scoped aggregate counts (Customers, Active Jobs, Staff) with Prisma, strictly constrained to the authenticated user's tenantId, and returns role-conditional payload arrays: Admin roles (SUPER_ADMIN, OFFICE_ADMIN) receive full metrics with recentCustomers, activeJobs, and staffByRole arrays while Staff roles receive a reduced payload. All responses use the uniform {success, message, data} envelope and every value is computed live from the database — never mocked.
acceptanceCriteria: Given no Bearer token or an invalid/expired JWT, when a client calls GET /api/dashboard/summary, then the response is 401 with the uniform envelope {success: false, message, data: null} and no aggregation logic executes (route is mounted behind the app's JWT Bearer guard).

All Prisma queries filter by the authenticated user's tenantId: when a second tenant with seeded Customers, Jobs, and TenantUsers exists, then tenant-1's summary counts are unchanged by tenant-2's data.
customerCount equals the number of Customer rows with the tenant's id and isDeleted = false.
activeJobCount equals the number of Job rows with the tenant's id and status = 'OPEN' (the documented default active state).
staffCount equals the number of TenantUser rows with the tenant's id and role != CUSTOMER.

When the caller's role is SUPER_ADMIN or OFFICE_ADMIN, then data includes customerCount, activeJobCount, staffCount, recentCustomers[] (top 5 Customers by createdAt desc, each {id, companyName}), activeJobs[] (top 5 OPEN Jobs by jobSequence desc, each {id, jobCode, name, status}), and staffByRole (count per role value) — the Admin payload arrays.

When the caller's role is STAFF, SALES_PERSON, PRICING_COURIER, PRICING_AIR_SEA, CS_COURIER, or CS_AIR_SEA, then data includes customerCount, activeJobCount, and activeJobs[] only — no staff metrics — the Staff payload arrays.

All values are computed live via Prisma count/findMany (no hardcoded or mocked numbers); an integration test calls GET /api/dashboard/summary with a seeded tenant (3 active customers, 2 OPEN jobs, 4 non-CUSTOMER TenantUser rows) and asserts 200 with the exact {success: true, message, data} envelope and expected counts/arrays, and a forced DB failure returns the uniform envelope with a 5xx status and no raw Prisma error or stack text in the body (sec-006).

The /dashboard route is registered in the app's single shared router config rendering DashboardComponent and appears in the route guard's allowlist (prefix matching); no second router or duplicate /dashboard entry exists.
Unit tests in dashboard.service.spec.ts cover the happy path (envelope -> DashboardSummary), the 401-replay path, and the malformed-envelope error case.

userStories.title: Implement POST /api/jobs with manual unique alphanumeric job code
userStories.description: Express route POST /api/jobs behind the existing JWT auth middleware, creating a tenant-scoped Job with a caller-supplied alphanumeric jobCode. The code is validated to [A-Za-z0-9]{1,32} and its in-tenant uniqueness is enforced before the insert commits, so a collision returns the standard 400 envelope rather than a raw error. Consumed by the Add Job modal on /jobs via jobsApi.createJob() from the jobs domain service.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/jobs with a valid Bearer token and body { jobCode: 'NM2026001', name: 'Freight to Rotterdam', customerId: <uuid> } returns 201 { success: true, message: 'Job created', data: { job } } and persists the Job with status 'OPEN', auto-incremented jobSequence, and createdById equal to the authenticated user id (sec-005 ownership binding).
A jobCode containing a hyphen, space, or exceeding 32 characters (e.g. 'NM-2026 001!') returns 400 { success: false, message } naming the alphanumeric bounds rule, and no Job row is inserted.

Creating a second job with the same jobCode in the same tenant (Prisma P2002) returns 400 { success: false, message: 'Job code already exists' } — never a raw 500 or stack trace (sec-006 P2002→400 mapping).

A request without a valid Bearer token returns 401; a CUSTOMER-role user returns 403 — only SUPER_ADMIN, OFFICE_ADMIN, STAFF, SALES_PERSON, PRICING_COURIER, PRICING_AIR_SEA, CS_COURIER, and CS_AIR_SEA may create jobs (sec-004 role guards).
A customerId belonging to another tenant is rejected with 400 { success: false, message } and no row is created (tenant isolation).
Integration tests POST /api/jobs with a valid payload (assert 201 and the { success, message, data.job } shape) and with a duplicate jobCode (assert 400 envelope with no stack text in the body).

userStories.title: Implement GET /api/jobs/:jobCode job header detail endpoint
userStories.description: Express route GET /api/jobs/:jobCode resolving a job by its unique code within the caller's tenant and returning the header data the workspace breadcrumb needs (job fields plus customer companyName). The response uses the uniform { success, message, data } envelope; unknown or cross-tenant codes return 404. Consumed by the JobsWorkspaceComponent header at /jobs-workspace/:jobCode via jobsApi.getJobByCode().
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/jobs/:jobCode for a job in the caller's tenant returns 200 { success: true, message: 'Job loaded', data: { job: { id, jobCode, name, status, isConfidential, jobSequence, customer: { id, companyName } } } }.
An unknown jobCode returns 404 { success: false, message: 'Job not found' } without revealing other tenants' codes in the body.
An unauthenticated request returns 401; a CUSTOMER user whose TenantUser.customerId does not match the job's customer returns 403, while staff/admin roles receive 200 (sec-004 role containment).
Integration tests: GET /api/jobs/<seeded code> asserts 200 and the data.job shape including customer.companyName; GET with an unseeded code asserts 404; GET without a token asserts 401.

userStories.title: Implement GET /api/folders/:jobId recursive folder tree endpoint
userStories.description: Express route GET /api/folders/:jobId returning the complete nested JobFolder tree for a job (recursive via parentId) plus root-level files, all tenant-scoped. Each folder node carries its files with exact sizeBytes and mimeType so the Angular service can hold the entire workspace in memory without further calls. Consumed by the /jobs-workspace/:jobCode tree and table panels via jobsApi.getFolderTree().
acceptanceCriteria: For a job with root → child → grandchild folders and files at each level, GET /api/folders/:jobId returns 200 { success: true, message: 'Folder tree loaded', data: { folders: [...], rootFiles: [...] } } with correct nesting depth and per-node fileCount matching the actual JobFile rows for that folder.
Every file entry includes exactly the persisted name, sizeBytes, and mimeType — no recomputation of these values in the API or the client.
A jobId that does not exist or belongs to another tenant returns 404 { success: false, message }; an unauthenticated request returns 401 (no tenant-crossing leak).
A CUSTOMER user may only fetch the tree of jobs whose customer matches their TenantUser.customerId; any other job returns 403.
All timestamps (e.g. file uploadedAt) serialize as ISO-8601 UTC with millisecond precision from the @db.Timestamptz(3) columns.

Unit tests build the nested tree from flat seeded rows (assert parent/child links and fileCount) and assert the builder terminates safely on malformed or cyclic parentId data instead of looping forever.

userStories.title: Implement POST /api/upload Azure Blob multipart file upload
userStories.description: Express route POST /api/upload accepting multipart/form-data (fields: file, jobId, optional folderId, optional createFolderName) and streaming the file to Azure Blob Storage (configured via AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT and AZURE_STORAGE_KEY env vars) before persisting a JobFile row. All blob processing happens inside the Node API boundary — the client sends the raw multipart body and never constructs blob URLs. With createFolderName and no file part, a new JobFolder is created under folderId (or the job root) instead, supporting the New Folder control. Consumed by the Upload File and New Folder controls on /jobs-workspace/:jobCode via jobsApi.uploadFile().
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/upload with a 1 KB text file and a valid jobId returns 201 { success: true, message: 'File uploaded', data: { file: { id, name, sizeBytes, mimeType, blobUrl, folderId } } }, stores the bytes in the Azure Blob container, and persists a JobFile with exact sizeBytes, mimeType, and createdById set from the JWT subject (sec-005 ownership binding).
A provided folderId is stored on the JobFile; an omitted folderId stores null (job root); a folderId that does not belong to jobId returns 400 { success: false, message }.

createFolderName with no file part creates a JobFolder (folderSequence = max+1 within the job, folderCode derived from jobCode + sequence) and returns 201 { success: true, message: 'Folder created', data: { folder } } — the contract behind the New Folder control.
A request with no file part and no createFolderName, an empty file, or a file over 25 MB returns 400/413 { success: false, message } with no raw error leak (sec-006).
blobUrl is always generated server-side from the Azure SDK result; a client-supplied blobUrl field is ignored (no client-side blob processing per section mustNotInclude).
Unauthenticated requests return 401; a CUSTOMER-role user returns 403 — uploads are restricted to staff/admin roles (sec-004).
Integration tests upload a small file (assert 201 + data.file shape, JobFile row persisted with correct sizeBytes/mimeType) and assert the missing-file and oversized-file error envelopes.

userStories.title: Implement auth login refresh logout and me endpoints
userStories.description: Add auth.controller.ts and the auth router to the Express API (apps/api) exposing POST /api/auth/login, POST /api/auth/refresh, POST /api/auth/logout, and GET /api/auth/me, implementing the sec-004 dual-token contract. Login validates email + passwordHash against the User model and issues an access token (JWT_ACCESS_SECRET, 15m) plus a server-persisted RefreshToken (JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, 14d) with rotation; refresh validates the stored token, rotates it, and returns a new pair; logout revokes the refresh token; me returns the caller's profile from the token identity.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/login with valid email + password returns 200 { success: true, message, data: { accessToken, refreshToken, user: { id, email, username, firstName, lastName, role, tenantId } } }; the access token expires in 15 minutes and the refresh token in 14 days, both signed with their distinct secrets (sec-004).

POST /api/auth/login with an unknown email or wrong password returns 401 { success: false, message: 'Invalid credentials', data: null }; unknown emails run a constant-time comparison against a dummy hash so response timing does not reveal whether an account exists.

POST /api/auth/refresh with a valid, unexpired, server-stored refresh token returns 200 with a new accessToken + rotated refreshToken; the old refresh token row is invalidated in the same transaction and can never be reused.
POST /api/auth/refresh with an already-rotated, revoked, expired, or unknown refresh token returns 401 and revokes the whole token family (reuse detection), never a raw 500.
POST /api/auth/logout revokes the presented refresh token and returns 200 { success: true, message: 'Logged out', data: null }; calling it twice still returns 200.
GET /api/auth/me with a valid access token returns 200 with the caller's user profile including role and tenantId; missing/invalid tokens return 401 with the uniform envelope.
All responses use the uniform { success, message, data } envelope (sec-006); every Prisma/validation failure maps to a 400/401 envelope with no raw stack traces.
Integration tests in apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.test.ts cover login success/failure, refresh rotation + reuse detection, logout revocation, and me (Jest + supertest against a seeded user).

userStories.title: Create shared router config with RBAC guard and living route inventory
userStories.description: Create the single shared Angular router config apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts with the RBAC AuthGuard enforcing the sec-004 role matrices on every protected route. The guard validates the localized .data.roles array on router transitions with PREFIX matching (a role allowed on /customers may open /customers/:id), redirects unauthenticated sessions to /login, and acts as the living route inventory: every route known at this point maps to its exact component. Later feature stories register their routes and components in this same file — never a second router.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts exists as the single router config; a unit test asserts no second router module and no duplicate route registrations exist anywhere in apps/web.

AuthGuard enforces prefix-matching role checks: a route with data.roles ['STAFF'] permits /jobs and /jobs-workspace/:jobCode for a STAFF session, while a route restricted to ['SUPER_ADMIN','OFFICE_ADMIN'] denies a SALES_PERSON session and redirects.

The guard reads the authenticated user role from the localized token payload; a session with no token or an expired token is redirected to /login with the return URL preserved and restored after login.

The initial route inventory registers: /login (LoginComponent, public), /dashboard (DashboardComponent), /customers (CustomersComponent), /customers/:id (CustomerDetailComponent), /jobs (JobsListComponent placeholder), /jobs-workspace/:jobCode (JobsWorkspaceComponent), /staff (StaffComponent placeholder), /profile (ProfileComponent placeholder), and a wildcard 404 route rendering the design-system 404 page (STORY-design-003).
Every protected route appears in the guard allowlist; a route registered in the router but missing from the allowlist fails a completeness unit test in router-guard.spec.ts.
Karma unit tests cover unauthenticated redirect to /login, role-deny redirect, prefix-match allowance, and the route-inventory completeness check.

userStories.title: Implement GET api staff directory endpoint

acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/staff?page=1&pageSize=25 with a valid Bearer access token returns 200 { success: true, message, data: { items: StaffDto[], total, page, pageSize } } where StaffDto = { id, firstName, lastName, email, role } resolved through TenantUser.userId.

An optional search param does a case-insensitive substring match on firstName, lastName, or email; pagination defaults to page=1 pageSize=25 and clamps pageSize to 100 without an error.
A CUSTOMER-role token receives 403 (the staff directory is admin/staff-only); a missing or invalid token receives 401 with the uniform envelope.

All responses use the uniform envelope (sec-006); Prisma errors including P2002 map to 400-safe responses with no raw stack trace; unit tests cover tenant scoping, role filtering, search, and pagination in staff.service.test.ts.
